welcome.title: Welcome to MemDiver
welcome.body: Quick 30-second tour of the workspace. Press Esc anytime to dismiss.

toolbar.title: Toolbar
toolbar.body: MemDiver mode (verification vs. exploration), session controls, settings, and theme toggle live up here.

sidebar.title: Sidebar
sidebar.body: Browse bookmarks, dumps, binary format, structures, sessions, and file upload. Switch tabs to see each.

main.title: Main view
main.body: Hex viewer when a dump is loaded, or dataset overview for directory mode. This is where you inspect bytes.

bottom.title: Analysis panels
bottom.body: Analysis config, results, strings, entropy charts, and more. Tabs vary by mode.

detail.title: Detail inspector
detail.body: Shows parsed structure fields, analysis summaries, or investigation context.

done.title: You're set
done.body: Next: try the 'Apply a structure' tour that will start after this one.

welcome.title: Welcome to MemDiver
welcome.body: Let's apply your first structure - takes 30 seconds. Click 'Next' to begin.

structuresPanel.title: Structure library
structuresPanel.body: These are structure layouts you can apply to bytes in the dump. Each one parses memory into named fields.

hexCursor.title: Set the cursor
hexCursor.body: Click any byte in this hex view to position your cursor. The structure will be applied starting there.
hexCursor.requireAction: Click any byte in the hex view to continue.

applyStructure.title: Apply a structure
applyStructure.body: Click the play icon next to any structure to apply it at the cursor.
applyStructure.requireAction: Click a structure's play button to continue.

overlayPanel.title: Explore fields
overlayPanel.body: The structure's fields are now color-coded in the hex view. Click any row here to jump to that field.

autoDetect.title: Auto-detect
autoDetect.body: Not sure which structure fits? 'Auto-detect at cursor' tries all of them and picks the best match.

done.title: You're ready
done.body: Re-run this tour anytime from Settings -> Run onboarding tour.

welcome.title: The Phase 25 pipeline
welcome.body: Five stages take you from raw dumps to a verified key and a ready-to-run Volatility 3 plugin. Let's walk through the UI in 90 seconds.

funnel.title: The reduction funnel
funnel.body: While the pipeline runs, this bar shrinks with each filter stage: variance → alignment → entropy → candidates → verified. A 192 MB dump typically ends at a handful of 32-byte candidates.

recipe.title: Pick a recipe
recipe.body: Recipes are pre-filled starting points. 'Replicate gocryptfs DFRWS' loads the thresholds from the paper so a reviewer can reproduce the published hits in one click.

oracleExplain.title: Bring your own oracle
oracleExplain.body: An oracle is a small Python file that tells the pipeline whether a candidate key decrypts your target. Shape 1 is a plain function; Shape 2 is a stateful class that caches setup cost.

oracleDryrun.title: Smoke-test your oracle
oracleDryrun.body: Before committing to a 9000-candidate run, click 'Test on 16 samples'. Mostly-red dots are normal — random offsets almost never decrypt. We're just checking the oracle loads and answers.

survivorCurve.title: Survivor curve
survivorCurve.body: If you enabled the n-sweep, each dump-count checkpoint produces a log-y point here. The curve mirrors the CLI's report.html exactly — it's how we claim reproducibility.

artifacts.title: Artifacts — the payoff
artifacts.body: The Plugin tab shows the emitted Volatility 3 plugin source. The Report tab renders the nsweep report HTML inline. Raw has the JSON + markdown behind a collapsible.

newRun.title: Ready to run
newRun.body: That's the whole loop: pick a recipe, arm an oracle, hit 'Run pipeline', watch the funnel shrink, and ship the emitted plugin. Re-run this tour anytime from Settings → Run onboarding tour.
